title: ARIA toggle fields need an accessible name
summary: A custom checkbox, switch, radio or similar has no accessible name. Label it with aria-labeledby or aria-label.
problem: An element with a toggle role such as checkbox, switch, radio, menuitemcheckbox or option has no accessible name. The role and state can be announced, but not what is being switched on or off.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear "switch, off" and similar with no subject, so they cannot tell what the setting does. Voice control users cannot target the control by name.
steps: Find the element in the scan result.
If a visible label is next to it, give the label an id and reference it with aria-labeledby on the control.
If there is no visible label, add aria-label with the name of the setting.
Prefer a native <input type="checkbox"> with a <label>, which needs no ARIA.
after: Email reminders
whyItMatters: A setting with no name cannot be changed with confidence, which matters most for privacy and notification choices. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Select the control in your browser's accessibility inspector and check its Name is filled in. A screen reader should announce the name, the role and the state.
